**Ephemeral** means lasting only a short time.

Think of a mayfly — it lives for just a day before it's gone. Or a text message that disappears after you read it. Anything fleeting like that is ephemeral.

It matters because it's a handy word for talking about things that don't stick around — trends, beauty, youth, you name it.

(Source: dictionary definition)

Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time. Think of a sunrise or a soap bubble — beautiful, then gone. It comes from Greek and originally described things that literally only lasted a day, like certain flowers or insects. You'll often see it used to describe trends, emotions, or moments that don't stick around. Source: dictionary definition.

Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time, or existing for just a single day.

Think of a morning dew drop on a leaf — there one moment, gone by midday. Or Instagram and Snapchat "stories" that vanish after 24 hours.

It matters because it captures that bittersweet quality of things worth paying attention to precisely because they won't stick around. (Source: dictionary definition.)

The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. Built from 1887 to 1889 by the company of engineer Gustave Eiffel, it was originally constructed as the entrance arch for the 1889 World's Fair. Standing 330 meters (1,083 ft) tall, it's the most iconic symbol of Paris and one of the most-visited paid monuments in the world.

The Eiffel Tower (Tour Eiffel) is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. Standing 330 meters (1,083 feet) tall, it was built as the entrance arch for the 1889 World's Fair to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the French Revolution. Designed by engineer Gustave Eiffel's company, it was originally criticized by artists and intellectuals but has since become the most recognizable symbol of Paris and one of the most-visited paid monuments in the world. Today it features three levels open to the public, observation decks on the first and second floors, and a champagne bar at the top.

The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. Designed and built by Gustave Eiffel's company between 1887 and 1889, it was originally constructed as the centerpiece for the 1889 World's Fair. Standing at 330 meters (1,083 ft) tall, it was the world's tallest man-made structure until the Chrysler Building was completed in 1930. Today, it's one of the most recognizable landmarks in the world and the most-visited paid monument, welcoming millions of visitors annually.
